images.caption: Figure 7:Additional Qwen-Image comparisons.Rows show strawberries in a basket, an astronaut riding a horse, and a fox in snow. The leftmost column is the 50-NFE reference; all accelerated methods use 8 NFE in the first two rows and 10 NFE in the last, with the measured speedup shown below each image. SpecKCast more closely preserves the reference colors and object structure, while the baselines exhibit color shifts, altered content, or degraded texture.

Figure 8:HunyuanVideo: “a bottle and a chair.”Frames 0, 40, and 80 for each method show differences in facial detail, pose, and bottle placement. SpecKCast uses 10 NFE (4.27×4.27\times), compared with 10–11 NFE (3.853.85–4.24×4.24\times) for the baselines. It avoids the severe facial blur visible in FORA and TaylorSeer and keeps the bottle in hand, although the subject’s appearance still differs from the reference.

Figure 9:HunyuanVideo: “a bicycle leaning against a tree.”TaylorSeer (16 NFE,2.82×2.82\times) and Spectrum (14 NFE,3.13×3.13\times) introduce an additional wheel-like structure between the bicycle’s two wheels. SpecKCast (13 NFE,3.41×3.41\times) better preserves the main bicycle geometry across the displayed frames, although the front basket is missing.

Figure 10:Wan2.1-14B: a panda drinking coffee with a zoom-in.Frames 0, 40, and 80 show subject appearance and scene layout. All accelerated methods use 8 NFE except SeaCache (7 NFE). SpecKCast achieves5.61×5.61\timesspeedup while avoiding the strong color and boundary artifacts of HiCache and TaylorSeer. TeaCache (5.64×5.64\times) and SeaCache (6.05×6.05\times) are faster, but TeaCache softens the panda’s detail and SeaCache changes the scene more substantially.
